name: Pakudha Kaccayana
dates_notes: Placed broadly among the early Śramaṇa teachers reported in Buddhist sources. No independent text or securely recoverable institutional history survives.
evidence_basis: Buddhist reports of the six contemporary teachers.
core_thesis: Pakudha Kaccāyana is reported as holding that seven ungenerated and unchanging constituents—earth, water, fire, air, pleasure, pain, and life—do not genuinely affect one another. In the Buddhist account, this ontology recasts apparently violent action as the movement of a weapon among fixed constituents rather than the killing of a person. The position is philosophically important as an early attempt to pair an invariant ontology with the denial of ordinary agency, but the report is hostile and no independent Pakudha text survives.
